en: Never leave aerosol spray cans in a hot car because heating the gas inside increases pressure and can cause the metal can to explode.
Pouring muddy water through a clean cloth filter physically separates large solid dirt particles from the liquid water to make it safer for washing.
Never mix bleach with vinegar because combining these two liquids causes a dangerous chemical change that releases toxic chlorine gas into the air.
Cooking pots have metal bottoms because metal is a good conductor of heat, allowing thermal energy to quickly transfer from the stove to food.
Water expands when it freezes into solid ice, which is why leaving a full glass bottle in the freezer can cause the glass to shatter.
Stirring powdered juice into warm water creates a liquid solution, and the heat makes the solid powder dissolve much faster due to increased molecular movement.
Do not eat food from deeply rusted metal cans because the iron reacting with oxygen and water to form rust can compromise the protective seal.
Keep rubbing alcohol away from open flames because its high flammability means it can easily catch fire and cause severe burns during a chemical change.
Always shake liquid antibiotic suspensions before use because the solid medicine particles naturally settle at the bottom of the liquid mixture over time.
Steam from boiling water causes worse burns than liquid water because the hot gas releases extra thermal energy into your skin when it condenses.
Oven mitts are made of thick cloth because fabric is a thermal insulator that slows down the transfer of heat from hot pans to hands.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar creates a chemical change that produces carbon dioxide gas bubbles, which helps physically lift stubborn dirt out of sinks.
